reports.summary: Interface versus implementation before porting: host-runtime 535/19402, shm-transport 152/1963, tokenizer 2/38, shm-native 29/1860 (pub items / non-blank non-comment implementation lines outside cfg(test)). host-runtime and shm-native are deep; shm-transport is deep; tokenizer is a two-function facade over the vocabulary table by design. The host runtime has no dependency on the product daemon (zero references), and shm-transport is its only transport adapter. No Strong candidate.

candidates.title: Remove the unused producer half of frame_channel
candidates.interface: `#[doc(hidden)] pub mod frame_channel`: 47 public items, of which connection, dispatch, ring_transport, routing, and runtime use `FrameSender`, `frame_sender`, `InboundFrame`, `OwnedInboundFrame`, `InboundEvent`, `OutboundFrame`, `DirectFrame`, `DirectSerializer`, `QueuedOutboundFrame`, `SenderQueue`, `ReadClose`, `RejectedFrame`, `CopyCounter`
candidates.implementation: the producer half of `frame_channel.rs`: `ProducerError`, `ProducerReservation`, `ProducedBody`, `LeaseTracker`, `LeaseClose`, `ReceiveLease::segmented`, and the matching `frame_channel/contract_tests.rs` cases (about 300 of the module's 616 implementation lines) have no caller outside the module's own contract tests

deletion_test.rationale: Deleting the producer half makes the complexity vanish rather than move: no production or test caller outside `frame_channel` constructs a `ProducerReservation` or a `LeaseTracker`, and the mandatory-ring refactor that removed the TCP channel left them behind.

candidates.rationale: Not Strong: a deletion of dead surface, not a deepening, so the interface metric does not apply. Recorded rather than done in U3 because the wave's rule is no behavior change beyond renames, and the property catalog carries records (`ring-a-segmented-inbound-body-has-no-production-producer` and siblings) that describe this exact dead surface and must be re-dispositioned when it goes.
candidates.follow_up: remove after U3 lands, together with the catalog records that describe the dead surface

reports.summary: Iteration 1 (commit b6b75c7b9475c13f7c94b52f0a13f00d442e22da on wave/u3-controls, report 80eb963fd1af9114d3670c4ee8a32aa25ee9fa474065511a164e7bdde95d6c66) judged the pre-decomposition tree; it is superseded here because the checker verifies every post-integration report against HEAD. This is the second iteration-2 re-run after a test-only change: the only file that changed inside the analyzed modules since the previous iteration-2 report is packages/shm-native/tests/mechanism.ts (+2 lines: the raw-addon readiness test sets `later = null;`, with a comment, before closing its later pair so that pair's trailing wake finds nothing to poll), verified by diffing the two analyzed tips over the four module directories; no interface or implementation line changed, every cited line number was re-read against the recorded analyzed.commit and still holds, so no candidate strength moves. Interface versus implementation after integration, iteration 2: host-runtime 652/21361, shm-transport 216/4091, tokenizer 4/98, shm-native 36/2095 (pub items / non-blank non-comment implementation lines outside cfg(test), recomputed against the recorded analyzed.commit with the same counting rule; identical to the previous iteration-2 counts because tests/ is excluded). host-runtime, shm-transport, and shm-native are deep; tokenizer is a two-function facade over the vocabulary table by design. The three iteration-1 candidates are still present in the tree: the frame_channel producer half (ProducerReservation, ProducedBody, LeaseTracker, LeaseClose, ReceiveLease::segmented) has no caller outside frame_channel; host_runtime::auth::compute_proof (auth.rs:119) and shm-native setup::proof (setup.rs:248) still forward every argument to shm_transport::setup_auth::compute_proof, and the merged transport's verify_proof (setup_auth.rs:63) has zero production callers while both adapters still do their own ct_eq compare; harness_closure.rs:1112-1145 still keeps private verify_safe_ancestor/owner_uid/mode_bits/hex copies of instance.rs:676-824 helpers that generation.rs already imports. The loop-created Speculative candidate (duplicated unsafe &'static Ring borrow at lib.rs:964-968, 1185-1189, 1083-1086) is unchanged. No Strong candidate; no structural change accepted. Re-recorded after eight further test-only changes, each confined to a test body or a test module: `host_test_ring_profile_names_one_geometry` (crates/shm-transport/tests/profile.rs) asserts the arena charge against the literal 134,217,728, the per-direction arena against 67,108,864, and the span bound against 2; `canonical_route_open_body_is_167_bytes` (crates/host-runtime/tests/protocol_vectors.rs) decodes the committed control header and compares its length field with the body length; `independent_openers_see_one_stable_coordination_identity` (the `#[cfg(test)]` module of crates/host-runtime/src/lifecycle.rs) spells the lifetime lock path; `every_artifact_hash_and_embedding_scalar_participates_in_the_fingerprint` (the `#[cfg(test)]` module of crates/host-runtime/src/synapse/bundle.rs) plus a literal pin in crates/host-runtime/tests/synapse_bundle.rs prove fingerprint coverage over every artifact, each external-initializer name, every scalar, and the numeric output index value; `manifest_digest_is_stable_under_key_reordering`, `manifest_digest_changes_when_any_field_changes`, `manifest_digest_matches_an_external_canonicalization_of_the_fixture_text`, and `launch_roots_participate_in_the_digest_on_their_own` (crates/host-runtime/tests/harness_closure.rs) cover the digest clauses over every manifest and node field including all three launch forms; `credential_fingerprint_matches_the_documented_derivation_across_rows` (the `#[cfg(test)]` module of crates/host-runtime/src/broca/subprocess.rs) compares generated rows including both Pi aliases, a multibyte value, and two non-UTF-8 byte values with the documented derivation over the raw OS bytes, and `canonical_row_boundaries_separate_adjacent_fields` encodes field-boundary pairs apart through the pure encoder; and `production_proof_matches_the_oracle_across_perturbed_tuples` (crates/host-runtime/tests/protocol_vectors.rs) compares the production proof with the oracle, including a multibyte daemon version, over perturbed tuples. tests/ and `#[cfg(test)]` items are excluded from the interface and implementation counts, no cited line moved, and every candidate stands unchanged.

candidates.title: Concentrate the &'static Ring borrow behind one Channel accessor in shm-native
candidates.interface: one `Channel` method yielding the `'static` ring for a side, carrying the single field-order SAFETY argument
candidates.implementation: three copies of `let ring_ptr: *const Ring = channel.<side>.as_ref(); let ring: &'static Ring = unsafe { &*ring_ptr };` with matching SAFETY comments at lib.rs:964-968 (reserve, to_host), lib.rs:1185-1189 (receive, from_host, added by the ActiveLease change), and lib.rs:1083-1086 (test); the invariant they rely on is the `Channel` field order at lib.rs:69-82

deletion_test.rationale: Deleting the accessor returns the same three lines to each caller unchanged; it is a pass-through that centralises a comment, not policy.

candidates.rationale: Raised by the iteration-1 to iteration-2 change that made ActiveLease hold ReceiveLease<'static>: the ownership is correct (drop releases, Ring::release is crate-private) but the unsafe borrow pattern is now duplicated. The test-only mechanism.ts change is outside src/ and leaves all three sites unchanged; grep confirms exactly three `ring_ptr` sites. Fails both rubric tests; only one adapter needs a 'static ring (host_runtime borrows with lifetimes), so no seam. Recorded as Speculative for visibility only.
candidates.follow_up: if a third 'static borrow site appears, fold the three into one accessor and one SAFETY comment
